Deliverable: hostile schedules — corrupted and truncated bytes, re-sealed forgeries, digest/field mismatch, approval presented for a different subject, superseded decision replayed, and a race between two conflicting approvals — each case pinning the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer.

FORGERY MUST RESEAL THROUGH PRODUCTION. A corruption probe that mutates a field without recomputing the digest and re-encoding through the production codec tests the digest check only, never the field check. Every forgery case re-digests and re-encodes so the payload is internally consistent and only the SUBJECT is wrong.

NOT in scope: transport boundaries, durable store faults, runtime/provider faults, scheduler/activation authority, closing the completeness ratchet, or anything under tests/fault/**.

Owned paths: tests/security/integrity-boundaries.security.ts (plus at most one sibling file if the 400-line split applies).

Verification: `pnpm test:security` — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code.
definitionOfDone: Every constant in the integrity subset has at least one BEFORE, one AFTER and one RACE case, with a positive case count asserted per constant so a boundary that generated zero cases reddens.

Every refusal pins the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer; where a codec layer and an authority layer can both refuse, the fixture is valid at the codec layer so the authority layer is provably the one that answered.

Every forgery case re-digests and re-encodes through the PRODUCTION codec so the payload is internally consistent — a test asserts the forged payload passes the digest check and is refused on the subject, proving the case is not merely a digest-mismatch in disguise.
No hostile case yields an approval, an admitted revision, or a truth class above UNKNOWN; asserted once across the whole file.

A mutation that drops one subject-binding check from a covered production boundary turns a NAMED test red, and the drill confirms the red lands on the intended assertion rather than on a digest or shape guard firing earlier.

`pnpm test:security` runs with its exit code captured separately and prints a count line strictly above the pre-task baseline; the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Consume the roster's `integrity` axis tag as the definitive subset; the roster owns the partition and re-tagging here creates a silent overlap or gap.
A forgery probe must reseal through the production codec — recompute the digest and re-encode. A payload whose digest no longer matches only ever tests the digest check.
Assert against the production surface, never a test helper that reimplements a codec, a digest, or an approval rule.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec. Do not touch tests/fault/**.

Their owner task-9aca4b0524a648f1841237b40d4e345b is WORKING with an approved 6-step plan, not DONE.

WHY THAT BLOCKS. This slice's rails say to consume the roster's `integrity` axis tag as the definitive subset and to assert refusals through the harness helper. Neither exists, so planning now means guessing the tag shape and the helper signature — what the stale-by-default rail forbids. A local substitute would be worse: five siblings share ONE harness, and a per-slice copy is how the layer-blind assertion it exists to prevent gets written five times over.

Take the roster's tag, not the count in your own description. Detail in #general msg-66310d34324a4ac1a22204fe6562f396.
